existing_roles.description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.
  
  
Company Overview
  
At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our employees around the world work to discover and bring life-changing medicines to those who need them, improve the understanding and management of disease, and give back to our communities through philanthropy and volunteerism. We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We’re looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world.
  
  
Position Brand Description
  
How would you like a career where you get to apply your best technical and analytical skills to bring complex, high-potency biologic medicines to patients? We are seeking a scientific leader on our Parenteral Product Network Technical Services/Manufacturing Science (TS/MS) team to drive the commercialization of lyophilized drug products, with a focus on antibody drug conjugates (ADCs), and to provide technical support for commercial lyophilized product manufacturing.
  
In this role, you are critical to the success of Lilly’s oncology and biologics portfolio. As a Global Product Steward and lyophilization process expert, you will hold technical ownership of assigned lyophilized ADC and other parenteral products from late-stage development through the commercial lifecycle, serving as the technical link between Product Development and our commercial manufacturing sites. You will ensure these products are successfully launched, reliably supplied, and technically well controlled across internal and external sites.
  
  
Responsibilities
  
As an individual contributor, you will work side by side with colleagues in Product Development, Manufacturing Operations, Quality, EHS, and Supply Chain, as well as with external manufacturing organizations. You will be a visible technical presence in cross-functional teams, mentor junior technical associates, and escalate significant technical, quality, safety, and supply risks to management with clear assessments and recommended actions.
  
  
**Key responsibilities include:**  

* Serve as Global Product Steward and subject matter expert for lyophilized, ADC and parenteral products, holding end-to-end technical accountability for process performance, product quality, and supply across all manufacturing sites, and serving as the primary technical interface between Product Development and commercial manufacturing.
* Advance lyophilization technology in commercial manufacturing
* Maintain the product technical knowledge base and lifecycle strategy, including process history, critical material and supplier knowledge, a product technical risk register, and a roadmap for yield, robustness, capacity, and site-network improvements.
* Collaborate with product development and manufacturing site for technology transfer, scale-up, process performance qualification/validation, and comparability activities (including lyophilization cycle transfer between freeze-dryers of differing scale and design) to support commercial launch readiness.
* Escalate significant technical, quality, safety, compliance, and supply risks to TS/MS management in a timely manner, providing risk assessments, impact to patients and supply, and recommended mitigation plans.
* Own the commercial control strategy for lyophilization critical process parameters and critical quality attributes, and maintain process understanding through continued process verification, stability and batch trending, and global product assessment.
* Partner with Product Development to ensure manufacturability of new ADC and lyophilized products, and to provide commercial manufacturing feedback that informs formulation, cycle design, specifications, container closure selection, and site selection.
* Author and review technical sections of global regulatory submissions, post-approval changes, and responses to regulatory questions, and support inspection readiness at commercial sites.
* Lead process improvement and lifecycle management projects, including introduction of new lyophilization, filling, and containment technologies and qualification of vials, stoppers, and other critical materials.

Basic Qualifications
  
  

* A degree in a relevant area such as Pharmaceutical Science, Chemical Engineering, Biochemistry, or Chemistry with one of the following:
* PhD degree with 5 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing, or
* Master’s degree with 10 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing, or
* Bachelor’s degree with 15 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing.
* Hands-on experience with lyophilization development or manufacturing (e.g., formulation and cycle development, scale-up, tech transfer, or commercial cycle support).
* Working knowledge of protein-based and ADC drug product formulation and aseptic fill/finish processes.
* Experience supporting GMP commercial manufacturing, including technology transfer, process validation, and/or deviation investigation and resolution.

Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to be employed in the United States. Lilly does not anticipate providing sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B or TN status) for this employment position.
  
  
Additional Skills/Preferences
  
We want you to bring your lyophilization and biologics expertise, commercial manufacturing experience, and technical influence to help launch and supply ADC and other lyophilized medicines.
  
  
**Preferred experience includes:**  

* Direct ADC drug product experience, including handling of cytotoxic or highly potent payloads and the stability and process sensitivities of conjugated antibodies.
* Background in lyophilized product development, including formulation and excipient selection, freeze-drying cycle design, and thermal characterization, and cycle scale-up.
* Analytical characterization of lyophilized biologics and ADCs
* Experience with container closure and critical material qualification, including vial and stopper selection, container closure integrity, and the interaction of materials with processing equipment.
* Product stewardship experience, such as serving as technical owner or product lead for a commercial or late-stage product, authoring annual product reviews or technical risk assessments, and managing multi-site process harmonization.
* Demonstrated leadership, influence, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to interpret complex technical data, troubleshoot manufacturing issues, and clearly escalate risks and recommendations to management.
* Preparation, review, and response to global regulatory submissions (e.g., BLAs, NDAs, or equivalent), post-approval changes, and support of regulatory inspections.
* Working knowledge of statistical design of experiments and analysis, and of containment strategies and occupational exposure limits for potent compounds.
* Strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across Development, Operations, Quality, EHS, and external manufacturing partners.

We’re also excited if you bring an insatiable desire to learn, to innovate, and to challenge yourself for the benefit of patients.
  
  
Additional Information
  
  

* Recognition and future promotion on the Technical Ladder
* 10–20% domestic and international travel to commercial manufacturing sites and partners (to be confirmed by leadership)
* Lilly is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

Lilly is dedicated to helping individuals with disabilities to actively engage in the workforce, ensuring equal opportunities when vying for positions. If you require accommodation to submit a resume for a position at Lilly, please complete the accommodation request form (https://careers.lilly.com/us/en/workplace-accommodation) for further assistance. Please note this is for individuals to request an accommodation as part of the application process and any other correspondence will not receive a response.
  
  
Lilly is proud to be an EEO Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, color, religion, gender identity, sex, gender expression, sexual orientation, genetic information, ancestry, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.
  
  
Our employee resource groups (ERGs) offer strong support networks for their members and are open to all employees. Our current groups include: Africa, Middle East, Central Asia (AMECA), Black Employees at Lilly (BE@Lilly), Chinese Culture Network (CCN), EnAble, Evolve, Lilly Indian Network (LIN), Organization of Latinx at Lilly (OLA), Pride (LGBTQ+ Allies), Veterans Leadership Network (VLN) and Women’s Initiative for Leading at Lilly (WILL).

existing_roles.title: Director, Quality
existing_roles.description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.

### **What You Will Do:**

* In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
* You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
* This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
* Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
* Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
* Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
* Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
* Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
* Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
* Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
* Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
* Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
* Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
* Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
* Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
* Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
* Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
* Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

### **What you'll bring**

* 15+ years of experience in product quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, operations quality, or a related engineering discipline, including significant people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading quality for complex, high-volume consumer electronics, wearable, medical-adjacent, or similarly reliability-sensitive products.
* Experience leading and developing teams across one or more of the following areas: product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, or sustaining quality.
* A track record of establishing quality strategy, operating mechanisms, and measurable improvements from early product development through launch and sustaining.
* Strong understanding of product development, design verification and validation, component qualification, reliability engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
* Strong command of quality and problem-solving methods, including FMEA, 8D, CAPA, SPC, GR&R, DOE, root-cause analysis, control plans, and process capability.
* Experience using engineering, field, warranty, customer support, supplier, and manufacturing data to identify systemic risks and drive corrective action.
* Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
* Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
* Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.
* A self-directed, pragmatic, and resilient leadership style, with a willingness to engage deeply in details while maintaining a strategic perspective.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field required; advanced degree or quality certification is a plus.
* Preferred qualifications
* Experience with both product quality and supplier or manufacturing quality, or demonstrated ability to operate effectively across both domains.
* Experience with batteries, electronics, sensors, RF systems, precision mechanics, adhesives, miniaturized assemblies, or other demanding product technologies.
* Experience leading quality for products that combine hardware, firmware, software, and cloud-enabled member experiences.
* Experience building or scaling quality management systems during rapid company growth.
* Familiarity with product safety, regulatory, compliance, traceability, and risk-management requirements relevant to wearable technology.
* Experience with supplier development, APQP, PPAP, SCAR processes, multi-source strategies, capacity expansion, or major manufacturing transitions.
* Experience working across multiple countries, engineering sites, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

### **Nice to have:**

* HW Experience
* Global distributor teams
* grown and org

### **Benefits**

At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

What we offer:

* Competitive salary and equity packages
* Health, dental, vision insurance, and mental health resources
* An Ōura Ring of your own plus employee discounts for friends & family
* 20 days of paid time off plus 13 paid holidays plus 8 days of flexible wellness time off
* Paid sick leave and parental leave

Ōura takes a market-based approach to pay, which may vary depending on your location. US locations are categorized into tiers based on a cost of labor index for that geographic area. While most offers will be closer to the starting range, successful candidates' pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, internal peer equity, and market conditions. We are not considering candidates residing in the following states: Alaska (AK), Delaware (DE), Iowa (IA), Mississippi (MS), Nebraska (NE), South Dakota (SD), West Virginia (WV), and Wisconsin (WI).

Individuals seeking employment at ŌURA are considered without regard to age, ancestry, color, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, mental or physical disability, national origin, protected family care or medical leave status, race, religion (including beliefs and practices or the absence thereof), sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. existing_roles.description:
**Company Overview:**

Prime Medicine is a leading biotechnology company dedicated to creating and delivering the next generation of gene editing therapies to patients. The Company is leveraging its proprietary Prime Editing platform, a versatile, precise and efficient gene editing technology, to develop a new class of differentiated, one-time, potentially curative genetic therapies. Designed to make only the right edit at the right position within a gene while minimizing unwanted DNA modifications, Prime Editors have the potential to repair almost all types of genetic mutations and work in many different tissues, organs and cell types.

Prime Medicine is currently progressing a diversified portfolio of investigational therapeutic programs organized around our core areas of focus: hematology, immunology & oncology, liver and lung. Across each core area, Prime Medicine is focused initially on a set of high value programs, each targeting a disease with well-understood biology and a clearly defined clinical development and regulatory path, and each expected to provide the foundation for expansion into additional opportunities. For more information, please visit www.primemedicine.com.

Prime Medicine is a clinical-stage biotechnology company creating the next generation of gene editing therapies. Our Prime Editing platform is versatile, precise, and efficient, with the potential to address more than 90% of known disease-causing genetic mutations. We have three programs in the clinic: an ex vivo cell therapy for an ultra-rare disease advancing toward a Biologics License Application (BLA), and two in vivo liver-targeting LNP Prime Editor programs, with more in development. We are a mission-driven team working in a lean, fast-moving environment.

**Position Overview**
=====================

Reporting directly to the Chief Technology Officer, the Executive Director of Supply Chain and External Manufacturing is a member of the Technology, Development and Operations (TDO) leadership team. You will own Prime Medicine’s end-to-end supply chain, from raw materials through clinical supply and commercialization, with direct accountability for materials management and for supporting internal planning and manufacturing needs. You will manage our external manufacturing partners, lead a highly functional lean team, and serve as the primary partner to Finance for TDO external spend. We are looking for a leader who embraces AI as a core part of how supply chain and external manufacturing run at Prime Medicine, from forecasting and materials visibility to partner performance and cost modeling. This role is for someone who thrives in ambiguity, is energized by building, and pairs strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

**Primary Responsibilities**
============================

* Partner with the CTO and TDO leadership to define manufacturing and supply chain strategy, including network design, make-vs-buy decisions, and partner selection.
* **AI-enabled operations.** Lead the use of AI and digital tools across supply chain and external manufacturing, including demand forecasting, materials and inventory visibility, partner performance monitoring, contract and cost modeling, and logistics tracking, as well as keeping the function ahead of new tools as they emerge.
* **Materials management.** Own materials management across the portfolio, including forecasting, sourcing, purchasing, and inventory of raw materials, critical starting materials, and components, so materials are available on time for each program.
* **Planning and supply operations.** Support internal planning and the manufacturing needs of each program; deliver labeling, packaging, shipping, and cell therapy logistics on time and in full; and resolve supply risks before they affect timelines.
* **External manufacturing and partners.** Build and manage a network of CDMOs, CROs, and critical suppliers, including contracts, governance, performance, and qualification of new partners.
* **Clinical and commercial readiness.** Ensure supply chain documentation and external site readiness support IND and BLA submissions, working with CMC, Regulatory, Quality, Non-clinical Development, Clinical, and program teams.
* Own TDO budget development for external spend, cost projections, and financial reporting in close partnership with functional leaders and Finance.
* **Leadership**. Lead, coach, and inspire your team of supply chain/external manufacturing professionals and indirect colleagues across TDO; foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaborative problem-solving and goal attainment

**Preferred Qualifications**
============================

* Bachelor’s degree in a relevant technical discipline; advanced degree (MS, MBA, or PhD) preferred
* 15–20+ years of progressive experience in supply chain, technical operations, external manufacturing, process development, or MSAT within biotech or pharma
* Direct ownership of materials management and clinical supply for clinical-stage programs
* Experience managing CDMOs and CROs, including negotiating MSAs and SOWs
* Experience with cell therapy and/or LNP or nucleic acid programs; experience supporting IND/CTA and BLA/MAA submissions
* Financial acumen, including ownership of operating budgets and multi-year cost projections
* Track record of implementing AI or digital tools that improved forecasting, visibility, or decision-making in supply chain or operations, and of changing how teams work as a result
* Strong change management, project management, and communication skills, with the ability to build trust with partners, Finance, and senior leadership
* Plus: lean, fast-moving biotech; ultra-rare disease or small patient population experience

**Why Prime Medicine**
======================

Your work will matter: our programs have the potential to be curative therapies for patients with no other options, and this role directly enables that. You will be part of the TDO leadership team, with direct access to the CTO and interact with other Executive leaders, and you will shape how AI is applied to supply chain and manufacturing at a company where it is a growing priority. You will have ownership from day one in building how Prime Medicine delivers for patients.

Prime Medicine is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, veteran status, or any other classification protected by law.

Location: Cambridge, MA | Reports to: Chief Technology Officer | TDO Leadership Team Member

The pay range reflects the full-time base salary range we expect to pay for this role at the time of posting. Base pay will be determined based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, skills, and education. This role is eligible for an annual short-term incentive award (e.g., bonus) and an annual long-term incentive award (e.g., equity).

Prime Medicine offers a comprehensive Total Rewards package with robust health, financial, and wellness benefits—including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, a 401(k) match, and equity programs—along with generous paid time off, wellness days, and company-wide recharge breaks.

Our commitment to employee well-being reflects our belief that when we care for our people, we strengthen our ability to put patients first and make meaningful impact together.

$295,000 - $312,000 USD

With a dedicated team of approximately 35 employees, Eden combines the collaboration and impact of a close-knit operation with the opportunities of the broader Metrie organization. We are committed to quality, customer service, safety, continuous improvement, and a workplace where our people can grow.

**Why should you work for Metrie?**  
With us, you’re more than just a number. We work hard to create a home for our Metrie family where you are empowered to be your best every day. Your contributions matter to us! We take pride in our culture of learning, ownership, and one team, and are committed to cultivating a diverse and inclusive workplace for everyone. Watch this video to see why our employees feel like they truly belong here: **Feels like a Family – YouTube**

**The role**  
We are looking for a hands-on manufacturing leader to join Eden Millwork as Plant Manager. This is an opportunity for a people-focused leader who enjoys being close to the operation, developing an engaged team and fostering a safe work environment while delivering high-quality products for our customers.

Reporting to the Director of Eden, the Plant Manager is accountable for day-to-day plant performance, including safety, production, quality, financial results, maintenance, continuous improvement and on-time customer delivery.

**Location**  
This is an on-site role based at Eden Millwork in Knox, Pennsylvania.

**What You'll Do**

As Plant Manager, you will lead the Eden operation and translate business priorities into clear plans, expectations, and measurable results. You will maintain a strong presence on the production floor, build accountability across the team, and partner closely with Metrie leaders and support functions.

**You will**

* Lead day-to-day plant operations, aligning production, scheduling, maintenance, staffing, materials, and resources to achieve safety, quality, cost, and delivery objectives.

* Coordinate preventive maintenance, capital projects, and equipment improvement priorities to minimize downtime and support production readiness.
* Lead, coach, and develop the Eden team, building ownership, collaboration, accountability, and capability across the operation.
* Partner closely with Sales to understand customer needs, demand forecasts and upcoming opportunities, aligning production plans and capacity with business priorities and delivery commitments.
* Partner with People & Culture on workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding, performance management, employee relations, and employee development.
* Lead practical continuous improvement initiatives that improve workflow, productivity, quality, and cost performance.
* Build effective relationships with customers and suppliers and respond quickly to operational, material, scheduling, or service issues.
* Provide clear reporting on plant financials and key operating indicators, including variances, corrective actions, and improvement results.
* Collaborate with other Metrie teams to share best practices and support broader manufacturing and business priorities.

**Who You Are**

You are a practical and experienced manufacturing leader who enjoys being close to the operation and working alongside the team. You are comfortable in a hands-on manufacturing environment where quality and customer commitments matter and leaders are willing to roll up their sleeves. You set clear expectations, follow through on commitments, and build trust through consistent leadership.

**You bring:**

* A minimum of five years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, with a strong track record of leading, coaching and developing teams.
* Experience driving manufacturing performance across safety, quality, production, cost and customer delivery.
* Experience using Lean, Kaizen or other continuous improvement approaches to improve safety, quality, productivity or cost.
* Experience with production planning, equipment maintenance and practical operational problem-solving.
* Sound business and financial acumen, including the ability to interpret operating results, budgets, cost trends, and performance indicators.
* Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and analytical skills, with the ability to turn data into practical action.
* Excellent communication and relationship-building skills across employees, customers, suppliers, and leadership teams.

* Experience in millwork, building products or a related manufacturing environment is an asset.

**What you’ll enjoy**:

* Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package- medical, dental, eye care and life insurance. Benefits start first of the month following hire date.
* 401k Retirement Savings Plan- Company match, 100% vested after 6 months.

* Career growth opportunities within Eden Millwork and the broader Metrie organization.
* A close-knit, team-oriented environment where your leadership can have a visible impact.

**Job Title:**

Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality Engineering (Burnet, TX)

**Job Description:**

**THE ROLE**

The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality Engineering is responsible for leading manufacturing quality across two Entegris manufacturing sites in Texas and translating global quality standards and quality priorities into consistent site execution. This role provides multi-site leadership to reduce risk, strengthen process capability, improve customer satisfaction, and deliver measurable quality improvements across the two-site footprint.  
  
The Senior Manager partners with site Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Product Development, Customer Quality, Product Quality and Quality Systems teams to embed quality ownership into daily operations. This leader is accountable for site quality performance, consistent implementation of quality standards, compliance with applicable regulatory, industry, and customer requirements, and the development of capable site quality teams. The role leads through site quality leaders and teams, establishes clear ownership and follow-through, and escalates risks and resource needs to North America quality leadership.

The hired individual will work on-site at our Burnet, TX location with some travel to our Decatur, TX location.

  

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* Translate global quality standards and quality priorities into coordinated execution plans for the two Texas sites, with clear owners, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
* Lead manufacturing quality across all two sites through site quality leaders and teams; clarify responsibilities, prioritize resources based on risk, and maintain regular on-site engagement.
* Ensure consistent implementation of global quality standards, policies, procedures, and best practices; maintain audit readiness and timely closure of findings at each site.
* Partner with site Operations leaders to establish quality roadmaps, objectives, and common key performance indicators (KPIs); conduct routine cross-site reviews and drive recovery plans where performance falls short.
* Own quality improvement plans that reduce defects, scrap, rework, cost of poor quality (COPQ), customer complaints, and manufacturing escapes, with site-level accountability for results.
* Partner with Operations and Engineering to improve process capability, product conformity, yield, and manufacturing performance through effective process controls and proactive risk management.
* Lead targeted continuous improvement and change implementation across the two sites; standardize effective practices and verify that improvements are sustained.
* Ensure timely containment, disciplined root cause analysis, corrective/preventive action, and effectiveness verification for significant quality issues; deploy lessons learned across all two sites.
* Ensure practical, sustained application of SPC, MSA, FMEA, control plans, APQP, PPAP, 8D, A3, and DMAIC methodologies, as applicable to site processes and customer requirements.

existing_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing Engineering, Imaging
existing_roles.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril's family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

**ABOUT THE JOB**  
  
As the Director of Manufacturing Engineering, your role encompasses the strategic oversight and tactical management of manufacturing engineering and systems to support both the development of new products and the scaling of high-volume production in Waltham, MA. You are charged with ensuring rigorous manufacturing processes are in place, resulting in the consistent delivery of superior quality products to our customers. Your leadership will also guarantee the fulfillment of manufacturing's capacity commitments while driving advancements in digital tools and methodologies to improve design, analysis, and execution. This role demands an innovative and adaptable approach to solving complex manufacturing challenges in a highly dynamic environment.  
  
**WHAT YOU'LL DO:**

* **Build & Lead the Manufacturing Engineering Team:** Recruit, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of manufacturing engineers and technical staff. Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across the organization.
* **Drive Manufacturing Strategy & Technology:** Develop and implement a long-term manufacturing engineering strategy aligned with Anduril Imaging's growth objectives. Drive adoption of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools to enhance efficiency and scalability across development and high-volume production.
* **Lead New Product Introduction (NPI):** Partner with R&D and product development teams to ensure seamless transition of new products from design to production. Champion Design for Manufacturability (DfM) and Design for Assembly (DfA) principles early in the development cycle to de-risk production scaling.
* **Scale Production Capability:** Evaluate, plan, and prioritize supply chain, production, and test optimizations to ensure the value stream can reliably meet production output goals. Develop business cases for vertical integration or supplier diversification where strategic partnerships will accelerate scalability.
* **Drive Continuous Improvement & Complexity Reduction:** Lead initiatives to improve yield, reduce cycle time, and lower cost across the manufacturing value chain. Drive commonality optimization, component and supplier rationalization, and process standardization to simplify production at scale.
* **Resource & Budget Management:** Manage budgets, staffing, and capital equipment planning for the manufacturing engineering organization. Forecast headcount and operational needs to support rapid scaling, including classified production environments.

#### **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field; Master's degree or MBA preferred.
* 12+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing engineering and operations, with at least 5 years in a leadership role managing manufacturing engineering teams.
* Demonstrated experience owning manufacturing value chains for complex electro-mechanical or imaging hardware — defense, aerospace, or adjacent industries strongly preferred.
* Strong background in make-vs-buy analysis, contract manufacturer management, and supplier development for precision hardware.
* Experience managing NPI and scaling production in high-growth environments with condensed timelines.
* Familiarity with optical system integration and test, precision assembly, or imaging hardware manufacturing.
* Knowledge of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools.
* Familiarity with quality systems (ISO 9001/AS9100) and PLM, MES, and ERP systems.
* Hands-on experience physically manufacturing hardware (assembly, soldering, machining, fabrication, etc.).
* Excellent leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
* Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

  

### **Benefits**

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you're supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. *For more information,* *Explore Our Benefits**.*

  

### **Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams**

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

* **No Financial Requests:** Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
* **Please always verify communications:**
  + Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will *only* come from an @anduril.com address.
  + Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.
* **Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:** If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
* **What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:** Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

### **Data Privacy**

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

  

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

existing_roles.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by *TIME* as a “Best Invention”, *MIT Technology Review* as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and *Fast Company* as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.

Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.

**Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.**

**Role Description**
--------------------

Form Energy is hiring a Director of Supplier Industrialization Engineering and Quality to build and lead the team responsible for the technical relationship with our supplier base, from first sketch through high-volume production, and for the quality systems that ensure everything that arrives at our factories meets spec. This role reports into our VP, Global Supply Chain and brings together two functions that have to move as one: the engineers who industrialize our components and equipment, and the quality systems and team that hold our suppliers accountable once they are producing.

Form's 85% domestically sourced supply chain was built for a battery chemistry with no existing supplier base, which means the industrialization playbook and the quality systems we need are still being written. You will set that standard: rigorous enough to protect a product with a 100-hour duration promise, and practical enough to work with suppliers who are learning our process alongside us. You will fly high enough to set the strategy and the org, and go deep enough to sit in a root cause review when it matters.  
  
*Relocation assistance is available.*

### **What you'll do:**

* Lead Form's Supplier Industrialization Engineering and Supplier Quality organization, growing a team of engineers embedded across battery materials, components, and equipment categories.
* Own the end-to-end industrialization journey for direct materials and made-to-spec components, from design-for-manufacturability review and supplier selection through tooling qualification and sustaining production support.
* Build and own Form's supplier quality management system, including PPAP, APQP, PFMEA, control plans, and SCAR/8D corrective action processes, calibrated for a novel battery chemistry with no legacy supply base to borrow from.
* Set the technical bar for supplier selection and qualification, partnering with Global Supply Managers to ensure our sourcing strategy is backed by suppliers who can deliver on cost, quality, and schedule.
* Own supplier process capability and yield performance, coordinating with Design Engineering, Manufacturing, and Reliability teams to drive root cause analysis and corrective action when issues surface.
* Develop the roadmap and staffing plan for quality systems aligned to relevant standards (e.g., ISO 9001, IATF 16949) at a scale and stage appropriate to where Form is today and where we are headed.
* Represent supplier technical and quality readiness within the Product Development Process, ensuring every component and supplier is qualified ahead of commercial scale.
* Partner with Supply Chain leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to align supplier roadmaps with Form's build plan and deployment targets.

### **What you'll bring:**

* Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials Engineering, or a related technical field.
* 12+ years of experience in supplier industrialization, quality, or manufacturing engineering, including at least 5 years in a people leadership role building and scaling a team.
* Demonstrated expertise across DFM/DFA, PPAP, APQP, FMEA, SPC, and structured root cause methodologies (8D, 5 Whys).
* Experience building quality and industrialization systems from the ground up, ideally in a hardware, energy, or battery environment without an established supplier base to lean on.
* Strong technical fluency to go deep with engineers and suppliers, paired with the executive presence to represent risk, tradeoffs, and strategy to senior leadership.
* Comfort operating across the full arc from early design concept through high-volume production and sustaining support, with the judgment to know which problems need a system and which need a phone call.

*#LI-Onsite*

*Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.*

*When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.*

*To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.*

*If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.*  
  
*Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will* ***never*** *solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.*

existing_roles.description:
EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions helping industrial, infrastructure and defense customers address critical power and operational needs. The company delivers integrated solutions that combine energy storage technologies, power electronics, software-enabled intelligence, technical expertise and comprehensive global customer support. EnerSys supports customers across communications networks, data centers, energy infrastructure, material handling, transportation, aerospace and defense — including applications where power continuity is essential. Serving customers in more than 100 countries, EnerSys helps organizations manage energy more reliably, efficiently and intelligently in complex operating environments where uptime, safety and resilience matter.

  

**Job Purpose**
---------------

The Plant Manager will provide overall leadership for the phased development, start-up, ramp-up, and ongoing operation of the new lithium-ion cell manufacturing facility in Greenville, South Carolina. This is a unique opportunity to build a factory and its organization from the ground up in a fast-paced, highly dynamic environment.

The role will evolve through multiple phases of the project, beginning with facility construction and operational readiness and progressing through equipment installation and commissioning, production launch, workforce ramp-up, stabilization, and full-scale manufacturing operations.

The Plant Manager will be accountable for establishing the operating model, leadership capability, organizational structure, culture, management systems, and performance disciplines required to achieve excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, people, and customer satisfaction.

This leader must bring broad manufacturing expertise in a high-volume, fully automated environment and understand the interdependencies across production, engineering, maintenance, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, finance, and people. The successful candidate will combine strong operational and financial acumen with knowledge of lithium-ion cell manufacturing and a demonstrated ability to build organizations, develop leaders, anticipate workforce needs, and establish strong relationships with employees, customers, suppliers, and business partners.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------------

**Factory Development, Start-Up & Operational Readiness**

* Provide operational leadership throughout the phased development of the Greenville facility, ensuring manufacturing and operational requirements are incorporated as the factory is constructed, commissioned, launched, and scaled.
* Partner with Engineering, Project Management, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, EHS, People & Culture, IT/OT, and other functions to establish comprehensive manufacturing readiness.
* Translate facility and project milestones into executable operational plans covering equipment, processes, workforce, training, materials, systems, safety, quality, and infrastructure.
* Ensure equipment, manufacturing processes, systems, organizational capability, and workforce readiness progress together so that potential gaps are identified and resolved before they impact production.
* Establish the operating systems, standard work, governance, performance metrics, escalation processes, and accountability required to transition successfully from project execution into manufacturing operations.
* Lead the operational transition through equipment installation and commissioning, qualification, production launch, ramp-up, stabilization, and full-scale operations.

**Manufacturing & Operational Leadership**

* Provide end-to-end leadership of plant operations with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, capacity, employee performance, and overall manufacturing results.
* Maintain a comprehensive understanding of plant operating processes and ensure effective integration across production, maintenance, engineering, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, and supporting functions.
* Establish a culture of operational excellence, disciplined execution, accountability, continuous improvement, and structured problem solving.
* Establish and continuously evaluate plant KPIs to identify performance gaps, determine root causes, and drive sustainable corrective actions.
* Drive improvement in manufacturing productivity, equipment effectiveness, reliability, throughput, yield, quality, labor efficiency, and operating cost.
* Ensure appropriate manufacturing systems, controls, procedures, and escalation mechanisms are established as production volume and organizational complexity increase.
* Champion Lean manufacturing principles and create a culture in which continuous improvement is embedded throughout the organization.

**Lithium-Ion Cell Manufacturing**

* Provide leadership within a technically complex lithium-ion cell manufacturing environment.
* Apply practical knowledge of cell manufacturing processes, automated manufacturing equipment, process controls, materials, quality requirements, and production risks to operational decision-making.
* Work closely with Cell Engineering, Process Engineering, Quality, EHS, and other technical teams to establish safe, repeatable, high-quality manufacturing processes capable of operating at scale.
* Ensure plant teams understand the relationships among process capability, product quality, yield, throughput, equipment performance, manufacturing cost, and customer requirements.
* Support the effective introduction, industrialization, and scale-up of new manufacturing processes and technologies.

**Financial & Business Leadership**
-----------------------------------

* Own plant operating performance from both an operational and financial perspective.
* Develop and manage plant operating budgets, forecasts, labor plans, productivity targets, capital requirements, and cost-improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrate strong understanding of the economic drivers of manufacturing and translate operational performance into financial and business outcomes.
* Partner closely with Finance to understand and manage manufacturing cost, labor, productivity, inventory, scrap, yield, capital utilization, and other key plant performance drivers.
* Evaluate significant operational decisions through both manufacturing and financial lenses, balancing immediate execution requirements with the long-term capability and competitiveness of the plant.
* Establish strong cost-management and financial disciplines as the facility transitions from construction and start-up investment to sustainable manufacturing operations.

**Workforce Planning & Organizational Capability**

* Build the plant organization in phases aligned with facility construction, commissioning, production launch, ramp-up, and future operating requirements.
* Develop short- and long-term workforce plans to ensure the plant has the appropriate leadership, technical, skilled-trades, professional, and manufacturing capabilities required at each stage of growth.
* Anticipate talent, capacity, skill, and leadership gaps before they become constraints to manufacturing performance or future growth.
* Partner closely with People & Culture to develop recruiting, workforce planning, onboarding, training, retention, employee engagement, talent management, and organizational capability strategies.
* Establish clear organizational structures, decision rights, accountabilities, and leadership responsibilities as the facility grows and becomes operational.
* Develop workforce flexibility and organizational depth to mitigate single points of dependency and ensure business continuity.
* Regularly assess whether workforce capacity and capability are appropriately aligned with production requirements, operating plans, and future growth.

**Leadership Development & Succession**

* Recruit, build, coach, and develop a high-performing plant leadership team capable of successfully operating at increasing levels of scale and complexity.
* Establish a leadership culture where leaders are expected not only to deliver results but also to develop other leaders and build capability within their organizations.
* Partner with People & Culture to regularly assess leadership capability, organizational effectiveness, succession coverage, bench strength, and future talent requirements.
* Build strong succession pipelines for critical plant leadership and technical positions and ensure appropriate development plans are established for potential successors.
* Identify and develop high-potential talent through coaching, mentoring, expanded responsibilities, cross-functional experience, and targeted development opportunities.
* Establish sufficient leadership and technical depth to minimize organizational vulnerability and ensure continuity as the facility grows.
* Create a culture where talent development and succession planning are ongoing leadership responsibilities rather than periodic HR activities.

**Customer, Supplier & Stakeholder Leadership**
-----------------------------------------------

**Position Summary...**

**What you'll do...**
---------------------

The Director of Continuous Improvement leads monitoring, assurance, risk intelligence, control effectiveness, remediation, and transformation across Last Mile Delivery's Trust and Safety pillar focused on risk operations. This role identifies improvement opportunities, assesses whether risks and controls are effectively managed, determines root causes, and ensures corrective actions deliver sustainable results. The leader will evolve traditional quality assurance into a closed-loop assurance model that detects systemic issues, drives accountable remediation, and validates effectiveness. The role also leads operational resiliency through process redesign, business continuity, data-driven insights, tech automation —challenging how work is performed and designing scalable, sustainable solutions.
  
**About the team:**
  
The Trust & Safety team supports Last Mile Delivery by enabling a safe, fair, and resilient ecosystem that ensures fast and reliable service. This team drives continuous quality improvement through data analysis, root cause identification, and leadership in quality assurance programs. They collaborate with stakeholders to enhance processes, deliver consistent service, and promote trust with every delivery. Focused on operational excellence, the team fosters a culture of accountability and innovation, ensuring high standards and reliability while supporting the overall mission to save customers time through efficient delivery solutions.
  
**What you'll do:**
  
**Lead Monitoring & Assurance** by building a risk-based approach that identifies recurring defects, systemic weaknesses, and emerging operational issues.
  
**Drive root cause and remediation management**, ensuring issues have accountable owners, action plans, timelines, escalation, and effectiveness validation.
  
**Build Risk Intelligence** using data, incidents, and risk signals to identify trends, emerging risks, and proactive recommendations.
  
**Assess risks and control effectiveness**, identifying gaps and driving sustainable remediation.
  
**Transform operations** through process redesign, standardization, automation, and AI.
  
**Strengthen operational resilience** by addressing critical dependencies, vulnerabilities, and failure points.
  
**Deliver actionable reporting and insights** on operational health, risks, controls, and remediation.
  
**Partner cross-functionally** to prioritize systemic improvements and drive sustainable solutions.
  
**What you'll bring:**
  
Proven leadership experience in continuous improvement with a strong focus on root cause analysis, control effectiveness, process transformation, and building operational resiliency.
  
Expertise in developing, implementing, and evaluating monitoring programs and processes to enhance customer satisfaction and operational efficiency.
  
Ability to analyze complex data, identify behavioral gaps, and recommend actionable improvements.

The VP, Quality is responsible for providing strategic leadership and oversight for all aspects of the organization's Quality function, including Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Quality Compliance, Validation, and Supplier Quality. This role ensures the effectiveness of the Quality Management System (QMS), drives compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and industry standards, and promotes a culture of quality throughout the organization. The Vice President of Quality leads and develops the quality team, establishes quality objectives, and partners cross-functionally to support operational excellence, regulatory readiness, and continuous improvement initiatives.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Direct and oversee all Quality functions to ensure alignment with organizational goals and objectives.
* Maintain and monitor the effectiveness of the Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring all quality requirements are met and appropriately reported.
* Assess existing processes and procedures, identify opportunities for improvement, and implement effective solutions to enhance quality performance.
* Develop, implement, and sustain quality systems and controls in accordance with GxP requirements (GMP, GLP, and GCP) and company Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
* Author, review, and approve protocols, reports, SOPs, product specifications, and batch records.
* Ensure ongoing compliance with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMPs) and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Oversee product testing and analysis activities to ensure compliance with cGMP regulations, SOPs, and quality standards.
* Identify technical and quality-related challenges and drive effective corrective and preventive solutions.
* Provide leadership and accountability for the review of data supporting method validations and stability studies, ensuring the accuracy and integrity of technical reports and summaries.
* Ensure the timely completion and maintenance of documentation supporting testing and validation activities.

* Demonstrate organizational leadership through effective communication, transparency, integrity, strategic thinking, and the development of high-performing teams.

* Demonstrated ability to lead, supervise, and motivate team members.

Dexter Magnetic Technologies supplies specialized magnetic solutions and components to demanding applications in the medical, aerospace, defense, semiconductor manufacturing, oil and gas, and industrial end markets. Dexter’s engineers solve complex customer problems with innovative solutions, winning business based on quality, customer support, and application engineering expertise.

For more information on Dexter Magnetic Technologies, please visit: https://www.dextermag.com/ (https://www.dextermag.com/).

**Job Summary**

The Division VP of Quality is the senior Quality executive for the Division and is responsible for establishing and executing the Division’s Quality strategy, systems, standards, and culture.

  

This position provides strategic leadership to ensure the Division consistently delivers safe, reliable, compliant, and high-quality products and services that meet or exceed customer expectations while supporting the company’s growth, profitability, and operational objectives.

  

The role partners closely with Division leaders across Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Commercial, Finance, and Human Resources to establish a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, prevention, and customer excellence.

  

This position also serves as the subject matter expert for the enterprise-wide Permag Quality Management System and related regulatory and certification requirements, including ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 13485, ITAR, and other applicable customer, industry, and regulatory requirements. In this capacity this position supports and coordinates quality systems activities at sites across the entire Permag enterprise.

  

##### **Major Responsibilities - reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions:**

  

**Division Functions**

**Customer Quality & Strategic Relationships**

* Establish a customer-focused Quality culture throughout the Division.
* Provide leadership for significant customer quality issues, escalations, complaints, corrective actions, and recovery plans in the Division.
* Partner with Commercial and Operations leadership to protect and strengthen key customer relationships.
* Identify systemic customer quality trends and ensure corrective actions address root causes rather than symptoms.
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**Operational Quality & Continuous Improvement**

* Drive measurable improvements in first-pass yield, scrap, rework, nonconforming material, customer complaints, warranty/returns, CAPA effectiveness, and cost of poor quality.
* Establish Division Quality KPIs and performance expectations.
* Partner with Operations and Engineering to eliminate systemic process variation and improve manufacturing capability.
* Champion prevention-based Quality and continuous improvement methodologies throughout the Division
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**Quality Organization & Talent**

* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Division Quality organization.
* Establish organizational structure, roles, competencies, and succession plans necessary to support the Division’s current operations and future growth.
* Develop Quality leaders and technical talent through coaching, mentoring, and targeted development.
* Establish clear accountability and performance expectations across the Quality organization.
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**Risk Management**

* Identify and proactively manage Division Quality risks that could impact customers, operations, financial performance, reputation, or business continuity.
* Establish escalation protocols for significant Quality risks and provide leadership with timely visibility and recommendations.
* Partner with leadership to assess Quality risks associated with new customers, products, technologies, suppliers, facilities, and acquisitions.
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**New Product & Business Growth**

* Ensure Quality is embedded into new product development, design transfer, manufacturing process development, and launch activities.
* Partner with Engineering and Operations to establish appropriate quality controls prior to production launch.
* Provide Quality leadership and due diligence support for acquisitions, integrations, new facilities, and significant business expansion.
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**Leadership & Governance**

* Serve as a member of the Division leadership team and provide insight regarding Quality performance, risks, trends, and opportunities.
* Establish regular Quality performance reviews with executive and site leadership.
* Present enterprise Quality performance, significant risks, customer issues, and strategic initiatives to Division and upon request to executive leadership and the Board of Directors.
* Influence organizational decisions through data-driven analysis, sound business judgment, and a strong understanding of customer and operational requirements.
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

  

**Permag Enterprise Functions**

**Enterprise Quality Strategy**

* Coordinate the development and execution of Permag’s long-term Quality strategy aligned with business objectives, growth plans, customer requirements, and operational priorities.
* Coordinate the establishment of enterprise-wide Quality objectives, policies, standards, KPIs, and governance.
* Provide input into strategic planning, capital investment, new product development, operational expansion, and business growth initiatives relative to the Quality Function.

**Quality Management Systems**

* Ensure coordination of Permag’s Quality Management Systems across all locations.
* Coordinate consistent enterprise-wide processes for audits, CAPA, nonconforming material, corrective action, change control, document control, and quality risk management.
* Maintain organizational readiness for customer, regulatory, and third-party audits.
* Serve as the executive authority for and quality-related regulatory actions.

  

Other duties and projects assigned.

  

**Qualifications**

**Education, Experience & Certifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering required; advanced degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive experience in Quality within a complex manufacturing environment.
* Significant experience leading Quality organizations across multiple manufacturing sites and/or business units.
* Demonstrated experience developing and executing enterprise-wide Quality strategies.
* Extensive experience with ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 13485, and applicable regulatory/customer requirements.
* Experience with ITAR and export-control compliance preferred.
* Lead Auditor certification strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience working directly with executive leadership and major customers.
* Experience leading organizational transformation, continuous improvement, and cultural change.
* This position may require access to ITAR-controlled technical data and services. As such, all applicants must be U.S. persons, as defined by ITAR, to be considered for this role. A U.S. person is a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, or individual with protected status under U.S. immigration laws. Applicants who do not meet these criteria will not be considered for the position

  

Salary Range: $220,000-$235,000 + bonus

We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including Medical/Rx, Dental, Vision, Flexible Spending Accounts, Basic Life/AD&D (includes coverage for dependents 100% Company paid), Short-Term Disability, Long-Term Disability (100% Company paid), Supplemental Life/AD&D, 401(k) with Company match, tuition assistance after 1 year, paid time off, and 11 paid holidays.

***Reily Foods Company has a passion for flavor and has been providing iconic foods and beverages that create meals and memories for over 120 years! Our products consist of New England Coffee, French Market Coffee, Luzianne Iced Tea, Blue Plate Mayonnaise, Swans Down Cake Flour, Tiger Sauce, and Carroll Shelby Chili (to name a few) and can be found in foodservice and retail locations around the country.***

The Plant Manager is directly responsible for leading and driving all operational activities at the facility to ensure consistent levels of production excellence are achieved and sustained while developing a fully engaged and talented workforce. In this role, the Plant Manager will provide clear direction and leadership to the plant staff through goal setting, performance and metric reviews, action planning and Continuous Improvement execution. Collaborating with all cross-functional groups within the organization, this role must maintain a clear focus on the tactical and strategic plans of the facility and ensure that they are aligned with corporate goals and objectives. Lead operational culture to ensure that we are an employer of choice and a great place to work.

**Responsibilities:**

* Champions and drives continuous improvements in key areas, such as: Safety, Quality, Productivity, Cost and Customer Service.
* Fosters a Safety First, Quality Always culture focused on operational excellence while developing direct reports.
* Develops a highly effective leadership team by applying high standards for selection, communicating, and delegating key responsibilities, establishing clear vision and stretch goals, and actively utilizing all performance, development and career tools to their full potential. Improves upon the capabilities of all plant personnel and develops a highly motivated workforce.
* Leads facility to achieve Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and uses performance data to drive improvement and provide optimal production performance.
* Maintains KPI scorecard within the key plant areas. Conducts KPI review meetings with the plant leadership team.
* Implements cost-effective control systems over capital assets, operating expenditures, and labor costs.
* Continuously improves site processes and technologies. Develops and executes upon a site capital plan, addressing both short-term and long-term opportunities.
* Controls and minimizes overtime labor costs, maintenance/repair costs, downtime and product re-work.
* Identifies and eliminates potential sources of food safety risk. Responsible for delivering site environmental, health, & safety performance. Works to exceed expectations for all internal & external audits, i.e., BRC.
* Act as liaison between plant personnel and corporate functions building solid relationships between these teams. Effectively communicates urgent issues both internal and external to VP of Operations and the site leadership team, as needed. Identifies issues quickly, develop action plans and coordinate team member activities, so that these issues are communicated upward, and dealt with quickly & effectively.
* Identifies root causes of issues and adept at developing and implementing corrective actions to prevent repeat problems.
* Follow all safety procedures and actively participate in safety training and safety system ownership initiatives. Maintains safe and efficient use of equipment, tools, and person. Reports any injury or accident immediately to supervisory and/or any unsafe condition.
* Supports and complies with GMP’s. Understands and follows emergency action plan.
* Supports food safety, quality, and legality.
* Ensures the operation is providing food-safe, quality products which meet or exceed all product specifications and regulatory requirements.
* Other duties as assigned.

* Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Operations or related field
* 10+ years of production experience, preferably within a food and/or beverage manufacturing environment
* 5+ years of Operational leadership with a demonstrated ability to successfully build and mentor high performance teams
* Lean Six Sigma, PMP, TPM or other relevant certifications
* Operational Excellence mindset with success meeting production KPIs
* Solid understanding and enforcement of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP)
* Understanding of major functions within the plant and the ability to work directly with all levels and functions
* Knowledge of GFSI audit schemes, such as BRC and SQF
* Highly organized with ability to multi-task, recognize priority and complete tasks in a timely manner
* Positive attitude and a team player that promotes collaboration
* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment
* Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
* Proficient in MS Office Programs
* Willingness and ability to work any shift, if needed
* Ability to lift up to 50 pounds
* Willingness and ability to travel as needed

**We offer a comprehensive and thoughtfully designed benefits package that supports the well-being, financial security, and work-life balance of our employees.**

* 10 Paid Company Holidays
* Generous Paid Vacation & Sick Time
* Comprehensive, Affordable Medical, Dental & Vision Coverage for you and your family
* Health Savings Account (HSA) with company contributions
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) & Dependent Care FSA (DCFSA)
* 401(k) Retirement Plan with company match and discretionary profit sharing
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and financial wellness resources
* Company‑Paid Disability
* Company‑Paid Life Insurance equal to 1.5× annual compensation
* And more benefits designed to support your health, wealth, and well‑being

Together, these benefits reflect our commitment to caring for our employees both inside and outside the workplace.

In addition, Customer/Government Property audit assistance and property movement tracking will occur under this group.
* **Quality Engineering Manager** – leading product quality engineering including Product data reviews and customer buy-off activities, Quality Auditing, First Article Report completions and reviews, and root‑cause analysis
